A quick, newbie question about Tor
I don't believe so - the phone tether should handle the encryption / tunneling etc.

I won't pretend like I'm a expert on any of this stuff, but it seems like the connection between the computer and phone would still be unencrypted, right? So if you have Tor running on the computer the connection is encrypted for every step between you and the website, but with Tor running on the phone the very last step, between the computer and the phone, is not encrypted. Like I said, not an expert, but I always enjoy learning

From what I understand about Tor, anyone 'watching', like your ISP, is able to see what content is being loaded but is unable to tell who is loading it once it's passed through the Tor network.

The basic way that I understood it is that upon entering Tor, your ISP can see who you are but not what you're loading. Once it comes back out on the user end your ISP can then see what you're loading but not who you are. But I'm just not 100% sure how this particular setup would work.

I think the best bet would probably be to contact official Tor support or look for official forums. I'll post the answers to this in this thread if you're interested.

That's pretty well it @VioletteVanadium - encryption starts where the TOR daemon is running - same as if you had a machine on your network acting as a gateway - anything upstream (where traffic originates) is in the clear, anything downstream (where traffic goes) is encrypted.

How you describe entry and exit nodes is pretty much dead on. The bit you miss is relay, where you are passing other peoples request through you system. Here the ISP knows who you are and that you are possibly acting as a relay, but nothing about the source or destination of those packets or who is sending/receiving.
I honestly hope so. Am going to find out from the team, if I can, via forum or support. It would be quite convenient to be able to activate it via shortcut on my phone on a per-need basis.

FYI be careful with Orbot :

http://xordern.net/why-you-really-shouldn%27t-use-orweb-anymore.html

Its semi important , but it depends more on your actual connections on the TOR network . Connecting via your own bridge is probably the safest bet:

https://www.torproject.org/docs/bridges

The reason being first off, TOR is pretty much just an outbound SSL connection. The way ISPs know you are using TOR is because of known TOR relays. Bridges are not typically supposed to be known, thus making it difficult to block them .

When you talk about tethering, you don't need to use Orbot. You are already using your phones connection, so its better using it from your actual PC . I believe orbot is only for the phone browser anyways although several upgrades have improved on that.

TL;DR just keep tethering and stick to running TOR from your pc for most effective use of TOR .
